title: Impact of SIA's Foreign Associates' Losses and Carrying Capacity on Provision of Essential Transport Services
what_it_is: Impact of SIA's Foreign Associates' Losses and Carrying Capacity on Provision of Essential Transport Services

sections.label: SIA designated operating entity
sections.summary: SIA became a designated operating entity under the CAAS Act from 15 April 2025 after the Transport Sector (Critical Firms) Act came into force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: SIA became a designated operating entity under the CAAS Act from 15 April 2025, after the Transport Sector (Critical Firms) Act came into force.

sections.label: SIA reporting requirement
sections.summary: SIA must report events or irregularities that may materially impede essential transport services, but foreign associate losses do not necessarily meet that test.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: SIA is required to report if there is an event or irregularity that may materially impede or impair the provision of essential transport services, but losses in a foreign associate do not necessarily meet that test on their own.

sections.label: SIA funding and reserves
sections.summary: SIA is a listed company funding investments from its own balance sheet and earnings, with over S$10 billion cash reserves and over S$3 billion undrawn credit facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: SIA is a listed company that funds its investments from its own balance sheet and earnings, and it has currently more than S$10 billion in cash reserves and over S$3 billion in undrawn credit facilities.

sections.label: CAAS assessment of SIA
sections.summary: CAAS' assessment remains that SIA's ability to serve Singaporeans is not adversely affected, and as of 30 June it held S$10.5 billion cash against S$10.7 billion debt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: What I can tell this House is that at present, CAAS' assessment remains that SIA's ability to serve Singaporeans is not adversely affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As of 30 June, it held S$10.5 billion in cash against S$10.7 billion in debt.

sections.label: SIA Air India stake
sections.summary: SIA holds 25.1% and does not control Air India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fact: SIA holds 25.1% and does not control Air India.

sections.label: Temasek SIA recapitalisation
sections.summary: In 2020, Temasek, whose capital is part of past reserves, underwrote SIA's S$8.8 billion recapitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, in 2020, Temasek, whose capital is part of our past reserves, underwrote SIA's S$8.8 billion recapitalisation.

sections.label: Limit on SIA cash to Air India
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government has satisfied itself that there is a limit, return threshold, maximum exposure and stopping point on SIA's further cash to Air India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has the Government satisfied itself that there is a limit on SIA's further cash to Air India, a return threshold, a maximum exposure, a point at which it stops?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This cannot be a blank cheque, least of all on a minority stake.

sections.label: SIA current liabilities and cash reserves
sections.summary: The passage states SIA's current liabilities within the next 12 months are under S$3 billion, well within its cash reserves of over S$10 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Its current liabilities within the next 12 months are under S$3 billion, which is well within SIA's cash reserves of over S$10 billion.

sections.label: Temasek portfolio value
sections.summary: The passage states Temasek has a portfolio of over $500 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Temasek has a portfolio of over $500 billion.

sections.label: SIA revenue and monthly losses
sections.summary: The passage states SIA's incoming revenue was almost zero and it was losing $400 million a month, $4.3 billion that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: SIA's incoming revenue was almost zero and was losing $400 million a month – $4.3 billion that year to be exact.

sections.label: SIA fresh equity and bonds issue
sections.summary: The passage states that even with support, SIA needed additional liquidity, so $15 billion in fresh equity and bonds was issued to its shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Even with the support, SIA needed additional liquidity and so, we decided to issue $15 billion in fresh equity and bonds to its shareholders.

sections.label: Improper motives and commercial decisions
sections.summary: The passage states that insinuating improper motives does not contribute to a healthy climate for companies to make commercial decisions serving Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: To insinuate improper motives that any particular investment does not provide or contribute to a healthy climate for our companies to make commercial decisions which serve the best interest of Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Air India capital call
sections.summary: The passage states Air India's open-ended capital call on SIA and possibly Temasek is of great interest to all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The question of Air India and its open-ended capital call on SIA, and possibly Temasek, is a question of great interest for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: 25.1% minority stake
sections.summary: The passage states this is especially because it is constituted on a 25.1% minority stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: Especially because it is constituted on a 25.1% minority stake.

sections.label: Foreign airline stake law
sections.summary: The passage states that by law, no foreign airline in India can have a majority stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: By law, no foreign airline in India can have a majority stake.

sections.label: Claims grounded in facts
sections.summary: The passage states members may ask difficult questions but claims must be grounded in facts, not exaggerated speculation creating needless public alarm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Members may ask difficult questions but the claims we make must be grounded in facts, not exaggerated speculation that creates needless public alarm.
